newsitem.title: CHINA: China selenium consumption seen growing steadily.
newsitem.headline: China selenium consumption seen growing steadily.

text.p: Chinese consumption of selenium is expected to grow steadily over the next few years from the current estimated 250-300 tonnes a year, a Hong Kong-based official of Sogem (Far East) Ltd said on Tuesday.
China produced around 130-150 tonnes of selenium a year, making it a net importer of more than 100 tonnes, Sogem's David Fong told a metals conference in Beijing.
Sogem is the trading arm of Belgian non-ferrous metals group Union Miniere SA.
Selenium is a grey non-metallic chemical element used in photo-electric devices, in making red glass and in certain electrostatic copying processes.
"Glass and manganese refining have been the largest consuming sectors, but they are also subject to big fluctuations -- especially for glass, when there are changes in colouring tastes," Fong said.
"We nevertheless expect China consumption to steadily grow for the few years to come, and (for China to) stay a net importer," he said but gave no details.
